card.name: Key noun in warning statements
card.fires_on: The noun or word right after a warning heading or a risk phrase, such as 'Cases' after 'Methemoglobinemia:', or 'severity' and 'severe' in adverse reaction text. Also the last digit of HLA-B*1502.

modes.label: Cases after warning heading
modes.description: The word 'Cases' or 'case' opening a report of an adverse event.
modes.example: ( 5.2 ) • Methemoglobinemia :<< Cases>> of methemoglobinemia have been reported

modes.label: Severity words
modes.description: Words describing how bad a reaction may be, inside a warning sentence.
modes.example: Immune-mediated adverse reactions, which may be<< severe>> or fatal, can occur in any organ

modes.label: HLA allele digit
modes.description: The final digit of the HLA-B*1502 allele name.
modes.example: HLA-B*150<<2>> is present in less than 1%
